messages:
jen (cs): Heads-up — HeliumRetail is seeing sustained 429s for their dedicated pool for ~45m. They report requests queueing and no visible scale-out. Their dashboards show active replicas stuck at 2, target concurrency suggests ~12 needed. :thinking:

maria (support): Got logs from the customer. I can repro in our staging by replaying their traffic pattern. Initial glance: autoscaler received surge probes but we see repeated 'attach denied' control-plane responses and a couple of imagePullBackOff events. Posting snippet:
```
control-plane: attach_request denied reason=capacity.attach_denied code=403 detail="billing_hold"
kubelet: Back-off pulling image "redwood/runtime:2026-03-01"
autoscaler: probe_timeout backoff=6s attempts=3
```

sam (eng-runtime): :eyes: Can you paste the customer's Dedicated config? min/max, probe policy, and warmPool settings? Also need node provisioning and attach metrics from the last hour (attach_rate, attach_failures, warm_pool_fill).

jen (cs): Config from customer dashboard: minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=50, scaleStrategy=probe_based, warmPool.enabled=true, warmPool.size=0 (they disabled pre-warm to save cost). They didn't have reserved burst.

maria (support): Repro steps I ran (staging): 1) replay 200rps burst for 90s against dedicated endpoint 2) monitor /metrics/autoscaler and /metrics/attach 3) observe queue and 429s. Result: autoscaler decided not to spin up beyond 2 because attach requests returned capacity.attach_denied with billing_hold. When attach fails, controller backs off probe cadence which delays scale decisions.

alex (eng-platform): Two parallel issues likely: a) billing hold preventing new attaches from succeeding b) probe/backoff logic + warmPool disabled -> even when nodes provision, pods fail to attach and autoscaler keeps backing off. Ops: can you grep control-plane logs for customer account id and billing webhook events? Also check registry pull rate limiting for the cluster (imagePullBackOff).

maria (support): I did. Control-plane shows: 
```
billing-service: webhook: account=helium-retail status=PENDING action=throttle
attach-controller: attach denied account=helium-retail reason="billing_hold" request_id=abc123
```
We also see a couple of registry 429s from gcr for the runtime image ~2m after the surge.

sam (eng-runtime): Ok—if billing_hold is the direct cause of attach denied, that explains immediate attach failures. But we should still avoid long autoscaler backoff cycles if the attach failure is transient/authorized to be retried. Proposed quick mitigations: 1) temporarily increase minReplicas to 6 for HeliumRetail (manual) 2) enable warmPool pre-warm for them (1–2 nodes) 3) short-circuit autoscaler backoff when request_queue>threshold (we can patch heuristically).

jen (cs): Customer will accept increase to minReplicas for now. They want ETA for a full fix. Any idea on how long to get control-plane billing hold lifted if it's legit?

alex (eng-platform): I can ping billing ops now — if it's a policy hold we need finance to clear; usually ~30–60m with manual override. If it's quota, could be faster to increase account quota. I'll escalate.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-273650-attach-billing. Assigned to: billing-ops, eng-platform. Priority: P1 (customer-facing errors).

maria (support): Action plan I followed and notes to reproduce for triage: 
- Repro commands (staging):
  - curl -X POST https://staging.redwood.test/replay -d @helium-burst.json
  - kubectl -n dedicated get pods -o wide --selector=customer=helium-retail
  - kubectl logs -n control-plane attach-controller --since=1h | grep helium-retail
  - curl https://control-plane.internal/metrics | grep attach_failures

- Observed metrics: attach_fail_rate rose from ~0.2% to 12% during the burst; attach_latency median 1200ms -> 6s when throttled; queue_depth spiked to 400 requests. Autoscaler backoff doubled probe interval after 3 failures and didn't re-evaluate until queue dropped.

sam (eng-runtime): For immediate customer relief I've drafted a short runbook: 
1) Increase minReplicas to 6 for helium-retail via admin UI (or API):
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://console.internal/api/customers/helium-retail/scale -d '{"minReplicas":6}'
2) Enable warmPool with size=2:
   curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/customers/helium-retail/warmpool -d '{"enabled":true,"size":2}'
3) If imagePullBackOff is present, bump registry concurrency for that cluster temporarily or pull image into cluster cache.

alex (eng-platform): I'll follow up with billing ops. If they clear the hold, verify attach success rate >95% and scale returns to expected behavior. If billing ops cannot clear quickly, recommend we apply the manual overrides above. Also we should track this as a platform bug: autoscaler should not increase backoff delay when attach failures contain billing_quota/denied metadata — instead it should surface a hard error to ops/cs faster. I'll file PLAT-XXXX.

jen (cs): Noted. I'll message HeliumRetail with temporary mitigation steps and ETA ~30–60m for billing check + 15m for minReplicas/warmPool change. Asking them to confirm if they want us to apply the changes now. :thumbsup:

maria (support): Follow-up: after ops cleared billing hold (10m), I retried the staging replay. Attach failures dropped to 0.7% and autoscaler incrementally scaled up to 10 replicas within ~90s. Queue drained and 429s stopped. Will keep monitoring for 1h and follow up with a short incident summary.

sam (eng-runtime): Great. Post-incident follow-ups: 
- Short-term: add a control-plane alert for attach_denied:billing_hold (to notify CS faster)
- Medium-term: autoscaler backoff logic tweak to avoid long stalls when queue_depth > critical_threshold
- Long-term: increase resilience for registry pulls and warmPool recommendations for customers with bursty workloads.

alex (eng-platform): Filing follow-ups and assigning owners. Thanks all.

jen (cs): Customer updated: confirmed reduced 429s and will monitor. Closing loop with them after post-incident doc. :white_check_mark:
